description: Free, open-source database client. No telemetry, no accounts, no locked features.
cfg.confirmDestructive: Ask for confirmation before destructive statements (DROP, TRUNCATE, UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE). Read-only blocking is never affected by this setting.
cfg.maxRows: Maximum rows kept in one result view across all loaded pages.
cfg.historyEnabled: Record executed statements in a local history file (secrets are redacted).
cfg.openRows: Rows loaded when opening a table.
cfg.policyTeam: Team policy layer (same format as `.rizomadb/policy.json`). Deploy it through managed VS Code settings; project and user layers can only make it stricter.
cfg.catalogTeam: Path of a shared connection catalog file (no secrets).
cfg.auditEnabled: Write a local audit trail of every statement (literals are removed).
cfg.auditPath: Audit file path (default: the extension's storage folder).
cfg.auditValues: Keep literal values in audit entries. Off by default so the log holds no data.
cfg.aiEnabled: Turn on AI assistance. Off by default: nothing is sent anywhere until you enable it and confirm each remote request.
cfg.aiProvider: API style: `openai-compatible` (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, …) or `anthropic`.
cfg.aiEndpoint: Base URL of the model API. Local endpoints (localhost) send nothing off your machine.
cfg.aiRedact: Replace literal values in your SQL with `?` before it is included in a request.
cfg.mcpAutoRegister: Offer the read-only RizomaDB MCP server to VS Code's MCP client when a folder has `.rizomadb/mcp.json` (made by *RizomaDB: Generate MCP Configuration*). Off by default; the database password is asked when the server starts.
cfg.language: Language of the RizomaDB screens and messages: `auto` follows the VS Code display language, or force `en` / `es`. Command and setting names always follow VS Code.
cfg.resultsLocation: Where query results and opened tables appear: `bottom` (lower half under the editor, default), `full` (the whole editor area) or `beside` (next to the editor).
cfg.groupByFamily: Group the connections in the tree by engine type (relational, document, key-value…).
cfg.environments: Extra environments next to dev, staging and prod, e.g. `{ "name": "qa", "protection": "confirm" }`. Protection: `none`, `confirm` (ask before every write) or `readOnly` (block writes). Add one from the New connection screen too.
cfg.pageSize: Rows loaded per page of query results. "Load more" in the results view fetches the next page on every engine.
cfg.applyImmediately: Save each cell edit as soon as you confirm it, without pressing Apply. On `dev` connections it applies silently; every other environment still asks first, and policies and read-only rules always apply.
cfg.codeLens: Show Run and Explain buttons above each statement in query editors, plus Run all and the connection in use.
cfg.highlightStatement: Highlight the statement under the cursor in query editors.
walk.title: Get started with RizomaDB
walk.description: Connect, explore, query and edit your databases in a few steps.
walk.connect.title: Create your first connection
walk.connect.desc:
Pick your engine by its logo; the usual host, port and user are already filled in.
[New connection](command:rizomadb.newConnection)
walk.explore.title: Explore your databases
walk.explore.desc:
Connections are grouped by type. Click a table to see its rows, columns, relations and DDL.
[Show the connections view](command:workbench.view.extension.rizomadb)
walk.query.title: Write and run a query
walk.query.desc:
Every statement gets a Run button above it. Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac) runs the one under the cursor.
[New query](command:rizomadb.newQuery)
walk.edit.title: Edit data safely
walk.edit.desc:
Double-click a cell, review the pending changes and apply them in one transaction. The guide walks you through it.
[Open the guide](command:rizomadb.openGuide)
walk.settings.title: Make it yours
walk.settings.desc:
Language, where results open, environments and protections.
[Open the settings](command:rizomadb.openSettings)
